subject: ScoutMed — 0–7d retention pilot, PII handling & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Asha Narayanan <asha@scoutmed.ai>, Anil Kumar <anil@scoutmed.ai>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: ScoutMed — 0–7d retention pilot, PII handling & next steps

Hi Asha / Anil —

Thanks again for the time earlier — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on your clinical use cases and regulatory constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so everyone has the same view: 

Summary of the call
- Goal: run a supervised triage assistant on clinical intake forms and clinician notes to surface urgent alerts.
- Data types: structured intake fields (name, dob, MRN), short free-text notes (possible PHI), and anonymized telemetry.
- Hard requirement: ScoutMed cannot have long-term persistent PII in the inference logs; must either be redacted client-side or held for a very short window for debugging.
- Residency: US-only processing preferred; potential requirement for particular states (CA) — you flagged legal confirmation.

What Redwood can offer (proposal)
1) 0–7 day "ephemeral" retention pilot: model inference logs persisted for up to 7 days, then automatically purged. For debugging we keep encrypted KV caches for no more than 7 days and expose audit logs.
2) Field-level PII controls: support client-side data redaction, plus server-side optional token masking for known PHI fields.
3) Residency: route inference to our US-only clusters and restrict backups to US KMS keys.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Asha: can you confirm whether ScoutMed is okay with a 0–7 day pilot window for logs for the POC, or whether you need true 0-retention (no logs at all)?
- Anil / legal@scoutmed.ai: we need the minimal data map (which fields are PHI vs non-PHI) and any mandatory audit evidence items. I attached a sample data-map template.
- Redwood (priyom): we'll draft a concise pilot Addendum with the 0–7d option and a tight SLA for redaction & purge.

Attachments: redwood-0to7d-retention-proposal.pdf (proposal summary), scoutmed-data-map.xlsx (template)

I'll follow up with a short proposed pilot Addendum by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Jordan

Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ScoutMed — 0–7d retention pilot, PII handling & next steps

Jordan — thanks for the recap, that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) For the POC we would accept a 0–7 day pilot window *only* if we get the following guarantees:
   - All PHI fields must be redacted before being written to persistent logs unless specifically whitelisted.
   - Any persisted KV cache must be encrypted with keys controlled by ScoutMed (bring-your-own-key).

2) True 0-retention (no persisted logs at all) would be preferred if it can be done without making the model debugging impossible. If Redwood needs ephemeral traces for the very first few requests to tune performance, we need explicit manual purge triggers and audit evidence when purges occur.

3) Residency: we require processing in the US; CA residency is not strictly needed, but legal will confirm.

I'll attach our initial answers to the data-map template and an internal checklist for security evidence. Legal will review the Addendum once you send it.

Thanks — Asha

Subject: Re: ScoutMed — technical note on PII controls and BYOK

Hi Asha / ScoutMed legal —

Quick technical note from our side to address the guarantees you asked for: 

- Field-level redaction: Redwood supports both client-side redaction (recommended) and server-side token masking. Server-side masking will replace tokens with deterministic hashes that are reversible only with a separate key and can be configured to avoid storing the original tokens in logs.
- BYOK (Bring Your Own Key): we support customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest. Keys can be restricted to US regions.
- 0-retention option: we can enable a strict no-persist mode where inference payloads are not written to long-term logs; ephemeral traces (useful for debugging) are kept only in memory and can be optionally dumped to a short-lived encrypted store when explicitly approved. Manual purge and audit hooks are available; we can include a one-click purge action in the Console and emit a signed audit event.
- Audit evidence: Redwood can provide exported purge logs, per-request metadata, and a signed manifest for retention operations.

I'll attach a compact draft of the pilot Addendum (redwood-0to7d-retention-proposal.pdf) that encodes the 0–7d option plus a 0-retention toggle for the POC, and a checklist of evidence items. Jordan — if ScoutMed agrees to a 0–7d pilot with BYOK and field-level redaction enabled, I'll prepare the version we can get signed for POC.

Cheers — Priyom

Thanks for the materials. A few items from legal review (high level):

- ScoutMed will proceed with a 0–7 day pilot provided Redwood commits to:
  * BYOK for persisted material and a documented key rotation policy;
  * Field-level whitelisting so PHI is never persisted unless explicitly approved in writing;
  * Signed purge manifests for any manual purge actions.

- We need a short Addendum that enumerates the permitted fields and the purge SLA (we propose 24 hours for manual purge requests during business hours).

- Please send the final Addendum and an export of the requested audit checklist. We expect to return a redlined Addendum within 3 business days.
